questions.question: Select why impedance matching is important in microphone systems. / a). To increase echo b). To reduce signal loss and distortion c). To increase background noise d). To change the pitch of sound
questions.solution_html:
• B. U/CO2
  • Explanation of Amplitude ((1 Mark))
  •  Relation to loudness (loud/soft sound).
  •  Higher amplitude → louder sound; lower amplitude → softer sound.
  • Basic Introduction of DVI ((0.5 Mark))
  •  DVI (Digital Visual Interface) is used to transmit video signals only.
  • Explanation of Bass Control ((1 Mark))
  •  Bass refers to low-frequency sounds.
  •  Circuit boosts/attenuates low frequencies to enhance depth of sound.
  • Explanation / Key Feature ((0.5 Mark))
  •  Image quality depends on resolution (number of pixels).
  •  Enlarging the image causes pixelation.
  • Role in Video Production ((1 Mark))
  •  Cameras and video tools are used to capture scenes, visuals, and actions.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: State why crossover improves sound clarity. / a). Adds noise b). Prevents distortion c). Reduces power d). Stores signal
questions.solution_html:
• B. U/CO3
  • Example for Amplitude ((1 Mark))
  •  Example
  • o Loudspeaker at high volume → large amplitude
  • o Whisper → small amplitude
  • Key Differences ((3 Marks))
  • (Any 6 valid comparison points – (0.5 mark) each)
  •  Signal Type
  • HDMI → Audio + Video
  • DVI → Video only
  •  Audio Support
  • HDMI → Supports audio
  • DVI → No audio support
  •  Connector Size
  • HDMI → Smaller, compact
  • DVI → Larger connector
  •  Usage
  • HDMI → TVs, laptops, home theatre
  • DVI → Monitors, older PCs
  •  Compatibility
  • HDMI ↔ DVI compatible using adapters (video only)
  •  Resolution Support
  • HDMI → Supports higher resolutions (4K, etc.)
  • DVI → Limited compared to HDMI
  •  Additional Features
  • HDMI → Supports CEC, Ethernet (in newer versions)
  • DVI → No extra feature
  • Explanation of Treble Control ((1 Mark))
  •  Treble refers to high-frequency sounds.
  •  Circuit boosts/attenuates high frequencies to improve clarity.
  • Advantages ((1.5 Marks))
  • (Any 3 points – (0.5 mark) each)
  •  High detail and realistic images
  •  Suitable for photographs
  •  Supports complex color variations
  • Role in Audio Production ((1 Mark))
  •  Microphones and audio tools are used to record dialogue, background music, and
  • sound effects.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Recall the audio file format that uses uncompressed audio data. / a). MP3 b). WAV c). AMR d). AAC
questions.solution_html:
• B K/CO1
  • Definition of Frequency ((1 Mark))
  •  Correct definition: Frequency is the number of vibrations per second, measured in
  • Hertz (Hz).
  • Working Principle / Circuit Concept ((1.5 Marks))
  •  Uses RC (Resistor-Capacitor) networks.
  •  Capacitors allow high frequencies and block low frequencies.
  •  By adjusting controls (potentiometers), bass and treble levels are varied.
  • Disadvantages ((1.5 Marks))
  • (Any 3 points – (0.5 mark) each)
  •  Large file size
  •  Loss of quality when scaled (pixelation)
  •  Not suitable for logos/graphics requiring scaling
  • Role in Editing and Post-Production ((1.5 Marks))
  •  Editing software is used to cut, arrange, add effects, color correction, and
  • synchronize audio with video.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Indicate the advantage of fiber optic cable. / a). High bandwidth b). More interference c). Low speed d). Heavy weight

  •  Used in audio amplifiers, music systems, equalizer
